question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Last night’s / Christmas party was fun. / I wish / you would come.
solution:
The erroneous part is option 1) i.e. 'you would come.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The error lies in the part 'you would come.'
 
• In the given sentence, the action 'Christmas party' took place 'Last night' which implies that the action took place in the past.
 
• According to the rules of tense,** '****I wish you would come'** should be used when incident is occurring in the present.
 
• Whereas, **'I wish you had come'** is used to indicate a wish for something that already happened in the past.
 
• Therefore, in the given sentence we need to use 'you had come' in place of 'you would come' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct sentence:__* Last night’s Christmas party was fun. I wish** you had come.***
